1. Corn cob rounds (two pieces), cooked sweet corn.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Each piece is about 3.5 cm tall. 20 cm² × 3.5 cm ≈ 70 ml per piece, so about 140 ml total.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Cut vegetable bulk density ≈ 0.6 g/ml. 140 ml × 0.6 ≈ 84 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Cooked sweet corn ≈ 90 kcal/100 g. 84 g × 0.9 ≈ 76 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two small corn cob halves on a large plate should weigh well under 100 g. About 84 g and 76 kcal is plausible. The cob core is less energy-dense than kernels, so the energy figure may be slightly high.
